methodology: Evidence recall is the share of labeled passages found in the top five. Document recall counts the right page even when the passage differs. MRR is the reciprocal rank of the first match. nDCG credits the first match for each label and nothing for repeats. Each question is embedded once without a cache, and that latency counts toward semantic, hybrid, and reranked search. BM25 makes no API call. Reranking asks a model to order 30 hybrid candidates, at most four per page, and its latency counts. Every mode returns five passages, at most two per page. Bootstrap intervals resample questions 2,000 times with a fixed seed. Answer evaluation runs the full pipeline, including the support review, then a separate judge grades each kept statement and check against its cited passages.
limitations: The benchmark is small: 32 answerable questions and 8 that should be refused. It is not a production workload.

The author wrote the questions and labels with AI help. The holdout results were seen before reranking was added, so the holdout is not blind. Treat these results as exploratory until someone outside the project checks the labels.
Each question lists only some passages that answer it, so the evaluator can score a correct passage as a miss. Document recall shows how often the right page was found.
An exact quote proves where text came from, not that it supports the statement. The judge is a model and may share the serving model's mistakes, so read its per-statement verdicts.
Latency comes from one serial run on one machine. It is not a load test.
The corpus covers Kubernetes 1.35 core documentation. Runbook cannot see a cluster or name its root cause.
